chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a woman called Umm Habeeb emigrated among them, and she was a circumciser who circumcised the girls. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw her, he said to her: 'O Umm Habeeb, is the work that was in your hand still in your hand today?' She said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, unless it is forbidden, so forbid me from it.' He said, 'No, but it is permissible, so come closer to me until I teach you.'

She said, 'So I approached him, and he said: 'O Umm Habeeb, when you do it, do not overdo it, i.e., do not uproot it entirely, but scrape it, for it is brighter for the face and more pleasing to the husband.'.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Umm Habeeb had a sister called Umm Atiyya, and she was a hairdresser (meaning a ladies' maid). When Umm Habeeb returned to her sister, she informed her of what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said to her. So Umm Atiyya came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of what her sister had said to her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Come closer to me, O Umm Atiyya! When you attend to the girl, do not wash her face with a rag, for the rag absorbs the water of the face.'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on female circumcision and hairdressing as professions?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of female professionals in the fields of circumcision and hairdressing, framing their labor as a legitimate source of income (khasasah) within the early Islamic community. It provides specific technical guidelines—such as avoiding excessive wiping that absorbs moisture—to ensure the procedures enhance the client's beauty and marital satisfaction, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical application of fiqh in daily social and economic life.
